column1: # Files in `addons/exmateria_effects/` that do NOT compile in a stranger project.
# `path <TAB> ticket <TAB> error signature <TAB> why`, read by
# tests/stranger/shared/{stranger_install,stranger_burn_down}.gd and by rig.sh.
# NAMED, NEVER COUNTED, AND CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A row says "we know, it is
# ticketed, it is goal #5 unmet on record" — the same contract
# `check_addon_portability.ARM1_BURN_DOWN` has. The arm fails if an UNLISTED file
# stops compiling AND if a LISTED one starts, because a burn-down that only grows is
# a list nobody ever deletes from. See `tests/stranger/README.md` and
# `tests/stranger/exmateria_battlefield/known_failures.tsv`, which is the same
# contract written out at length.
# THE SIGNATURE COLUMN IS LOAD-BEARING. A broken script throws when ANY script that
# names it is loaded, so the rig cannot simply not-look: it has to be able to say
# which throws this list already explains. The signature is the substring of the
# engine's own parse error, and a `SCRIPT ERROR` line matching no signature is still
# the finding. `Failed to compile depended scripts` is allowed unconditionally — it
# is a cascade line naming no file and no symbol.
# 🟢 THIS FILE IS EMPTY, AND IT OPENED WITH TWENTY-ONE ROWS ON 2026-09-12 — the
# day #1225 moved extraction #7 in. 21 -> 6 -> 5 -> 2 -> 0, all on the same date, and
# the drain is the point: the two rigs written before this one were authored AFTER
# their addons were already installable, so both files have always been empty and
# neither could ever show a burn-down being WATCHED rather than asserted. ADR-0192
# dec. 1 says the register goes FIRST; this is that rule applied to a rig, and the
# sequence is what it bought.
# WHO PAID WHAT, because "it went to zero" is not a record:
#   #1218  fifteen rows — 61 `Debug.DebugConfig` reads re-pointed at `install/EffectsDebug.gd`
#   #1219  the sixteenth — `cast/EffectManager.gd`'s three `Unit` annotations
#   #1225  three — the addon's OWN autoloads (`TintedSurfaces`, `ScreenEffectOverlay`)
#          through two in-addon ports; ADR-0310. Those three rows each asserted in
#          prose that NOTHING COULD PAY THEM, naming two real consumer-side routes and
#          missing a third that was entirely this addon's — which this rig printed, in
#          this file, a few lines from the denial.
#   #1286  the last two — `exmateria_sound`, declared in `deps=` at last.
# 🔴 AND THE LAST TWO WERE NEVER THIS ADDON'S DEFECT AT ALL. They were four
# `preload`s into `addons/exmateria_sound/`, a package the rig did not stage — and the
# reason it did not was two missing `plugin.cfg` keys over in `exmateria-sound/`, not
# anything wrong here. Declaring the dep printed `CANNOT RUN: … declares no engine=`;
# #1286 measured and added `engine="stock"` to both sound addons (zero fork primitives
# in either, and that package's own rigs already booted `$GODOT_STOCK` 30 times and
# `$GODOT_FORK` never) plus `deps="exmateria_spu"`. The rig then staged a SEVEN-addon
# closure and both files compiled on the first run. Staging was never the blocker:
# `rig.sh` stages `$PKG/addons/<name>` and `godot-learning/addons/exmateria_sound` has
# been a symlink into the package all along.
# 🔴 THE GENERAL LESSON, AND IT COST TWO RE-TICKETS AND A CLOSED TICKET TO LEARN:
# **"nothing can pay this" is the single claim in a burn-down row most worth
# re-deriving before believing.** A `why` column is unverifiable prose by construction
# — the rig checks the PATH and the SIGNATURE and nothing else — so a row asserting it
# is unpayable is a row nobody tries to pay. Three rows said it and were wrong about
# the route; two more said it and were right about the blocker but wrong that it was
# out of reach. Both readings survived because each was re-ticketed instead of
# CLOSED the whole time — #1276's finding on a third register).
# 🔴 A ZERO HERE IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS, AND THE TWO EXCLUSIONS ARE BY
# CONSTRUCTION. This file says every member PARSES in a project that did nothing for
# this addon beyond unzipping its declared closure. It does NOT say:
#   * that LOAD-time reaches resolve. The eight `res://assets/` literals addressing the
#     ROM-derived content pack are `FileAccess`/`ResourceLoader` calls, so every file
#     holding one compiles in a project with no `assets/` at all and this rig reports
#     nothing about them. They are declared where they CAN be seen —
#     `check_addon_install.py`'s Class B rows and `check_addon_portability.py`'s
#     ARM6_BURN_DOWN. A rig's silence is not a measurement (ADR-0194 dec. 12).
#   * that the addon RUNS. `plugin.gd` is deliberately not enabled here, because
#     enabling is an EDITOR action and a rig that enabled it would be measuring the
#     editor rather than the install.
# HOW TO PUT A ROW BACK. A new row is `path <TAB> ticket <TAB> signature <TAB> why`, and
# the arm fails in BOTH directions — an UNLISTED file that stops compiling, and a LISTED
# one that starts — so a row cannot be parked here and forgotten. Do not let an empty
# file become an unread one: `tests/stranger/exmateria_battlefield/known_failures.tsv`
# is the same contract written out at length.
